title: Signed shifts of an already normalized tensor comparison
statement: Fix a universe u, categories C,D with objects in Type (u+1) and morphisms in Type u, Grothendieck topologies J,K, ring sheaves R on J and S on K valued in CommRingCat (u+1), and a site functor F:C to D. Let o:Operation F R S be exact, and let a,b be the resolving tensor models of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction-data], with normalized shifts sa,sb. Given an ordinary tensor comparison mu satisfying its pure-unit equation and an already constructed TensorComparison t for o.leftModel, normalized on every resolving pair, both TensorComparisonShifts equations hold for the canonical exact-derived shift. Only the two shift squares are asserted: no ordinary, chain or derived comparison is constructed.

proof.text: Use the pure-unit equation and the module adjunction to prove naturality of the supplied ordinary tensor isomorphisms, testing on pure tensors. Package them as a natural isomorphism of curried bifunctors. Apply the proved source-library mapBifunctorComparisonNatTrans construction. Pullback is a left adjoint, so this chain comparison is invertible; its inverse agrees with the prescribed totalMap, as checked on each coproduct inclusion.

For each fixed resolving complex, package the tensor representative isomorphisms as a natural isomorphism in the other resolving complex. The supplied first and second normalization equations prove that these natural isomorphisms commute with integer shifts. The same normalization fields imply shift stability of the resolving subcategories. The source-library commShift_mapBifunctorComparisonNatTrans_app and flipApp instances give both chain comparison squares, with the canonical unsigned first shift and Koszul-signed second shift.

Rewrite the representative equation of t by cancelling the inverse chain comparison and the target representative inverse. For a fixed resolving argument, its resulting square expresses the restriction of t as a conjugate of the localized chain comparison by representative and exact-derived factor isomorphisms. Every other edge commutes with shifts, including the exact-derived factor map; hence the restricted t does too.

The resolving subcategory followed by Q is essentially surjective: take a flat-term K-flat resolution of a complex representative of each derived object, transfer tensorRight exactness to site flatness through siteSheafTensorRightIso, and localize the quasi-isomorphism. NatTrans.CommShift.of_whiskerLeft therefore extends each restricted shift square to the whole varying derived category. Finally transport the fixed resolving argument to an arbitrary derived object along its representative isomorphism; naturality of t and the bifunctor shift structure preserves the square. Read off the two component equations. This argument needs no bound, nonzero ring, or nonempty site.

mathlib_searches.query: An exact derived pullback comparison for tensor products commutes with integer shifts when its tensor representatives and shift isomorphisms are normalized
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits. Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.ExactFunctor supplies the CommShift instance for mapDerivedCategory and NatTrans.CommShift for mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom. Other hits concern pullback of shifts and totalShift₂XIso. The factor compatibility is used in the argument; no hit proves both tensor comparison squares for arbitrary normalized resolving models.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Use the canonical exact-derived factors shift instance, together with tensor normalization, chain shift calculations and faithful restriction; no match for the whole statement.
